cards.subject: The eastern Barrens
lines: This ground had no name of its own. It was the edge of the Barrens, held by quilboar.
Thrall chose it because the rock was red and cracked and dry, and it looked like Draenor.

cards.subject: Durotan
lines: His father, assassinated by Gul'dan's agents when Thrall was a newborn. The killers cut off his arms so he could not hold his son.
Durotan was a Frostwolf. A chieftain of snow and ice.
Thrall named the hottest, driest red rock in Kalimdor after him.

cards.subject: The Valley of Trials
cards.tag: A demon cult in the nursery
lines: The first place any orc stands in the world has the Burning Blade living in caves at the north end of it.
It is a proving ground and the terms are not softened: those who fail are left to bake in the sun.
There is exactly one way out.

cards.subject: They cannot find them
lines: Cells in the starting valley, cells at Skull Rock, cells burning Thunder Ridge. Skull Rock is only one of several holdouts.
There is an orc at Razor Hill whose whole job is investigating them, and he never catches up.
The zone's real antagonist is a demon cult the Horde cannot get out of its own front yard.

cards.subject: Thunder Ridge
lines: Ancient forest, with herds of thunder lizards living in it.
Kul Tiras loggers cut it and the Burning Blade finished the job with demonic magic.
What is left is bare ridge and lizards with nowhere to be.

cards.subject: Razor Hill
lines: It is not named after anybody. The name comes from the terrain.
There were two separate things here in Warcraft III — a meeting point and a barracks north of it — and they were probably merged into one town.
Its biggest building is still the barracks.

cards.subject: Tiragarde Keep
cards.tag: Taking orders from a dead man
lines: Daelin Proudmoore built it during his invasion, in breach of the peace. The Horde killed him and took it.
It is still garrisoned. An officer found special orders among the dead admiral's effects and came back to hold the ruins.
Kul Tiras marines are patrolling crumbling walls on the Horde's own coast, prosecuting a war whose commander died years ago.

cards.subject: Sen'jin Village
cards.tag: A refugee camp with a father's name
lines: Sen'jin was Vol'jin's father. He died saving his people from murlocs, and Vol'jin named the village for him.
It is not a home. It is where the Darkspear ended up.
Three very small huts, two small huts, one big one, and a dock.

cards.subject: Zalazane
lines: The witch doctor who enslaved the Darkspear with voodoo and drove them onto the mainland is alive, on the main isle, surrounded by undead trolls.
He fooled adventurers for years — the heads brought back were painted rocks, coconuts, or an enslaved Darkspear's.
Nothing in this game kills him. The Isles are not retaken.

cards.subject: You have to swim
cards.tag: No boat, no flight path, no quest hub
lines: There is no way to the Echo Isles except into the water.
Most players leave Durotar at ten and never once look south from the dock.
The Darkspear can see the home they lost from their own beach, every day.

cards.subject: The coast nobody walks
lines: The levelling road never touches the water. People run it and leave.
The two most interesting things in this zone — an Alliance keep and a traitor's island — are both out on a shore most Horde characters never see.
There is almost nothing here that casts a shadow. Orgrimmar's walls are the first real shade in the zone.
